evals.name: opt-design-log-review
evals.prompt: I just ran opt_design. Can you analyze what it did and whether the optimizations were effective?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts opt_design section from log, reports per-phase stats (retarget/propconst/sweep/BUFG/carry remap), and gives directive recommendations.

assertions.name: log_scoped_correctly
assertions.description: Log extraction was scoped to the opt_design section only
assertions.check: Agent used sed -n '/Command: opt_design/,/opt_design: Time/p' or equivalent scoping

assertions.name: phase_stats_extracted
assertions.description: Per-phase optimization stats were reported
assertions.check: Output includes counts for retarget, propconst, sweep, or remap phases

assertions.name: change_summary_found
assertions.description: Opt_design Change Summary table was extracted
assertions.check: Output references the Change Summary showing before/after resource counts

assertions.name: session_id_passed
assertions.description: session_id was passed to all vivado_execute calls
assertions.check: Every vivado_execute call includes session_id

evals.name: dont-touch-conflicts
evals.prompt: opt_design seems to be skipping some optimizations. I have DONT_TOUCH and MARK_DEBUG on some signals. Can you check if those are blocking opt_design?
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies DONT_TOUCH/MARK_DEBUG properties in the opt_design log section, reports which optimizations were skipped, and recommends resolution.

assertions.name: blocking_props_identified
assertions.description: DONT_TOUCH/MARK_DEBUG blocking properties found in log
assertions.check: Output lists specific cells/nets with DONT_TOUCH or MARK_DEBUG that blocked optimization

assertions.name: session_id_passed
assertions.description: session_id was passed to all vivado_execute calls
assertions.check: Every vivado_execute call includes session_id

evals.name: muxf-optimization-analysis
evals.prompt: opt_design ran MUXF optimization. I'm seeing MUXF7 and MUXF8 being removed. Is that expected? What do the Opt 31-1384 through 31-1389 messages mean?
evals.expected_output: Agent explains MUXF optimization phase, reports per-type MUXF7/F8/F9 creation/removal stats from [Opt 31-1384]-[Opt 31-1389], and notes that removals indicate synthesis MUXF inference was aggressive.

assertions.name: muxf_ids_recognized
assertions.description: Agent recognizes [Opt 31-1384] through [Opt 31-1389] as MUXF per-type stats
assertions.check: Output mentions MUXF7/F8/F9 optimization stats and references the specific message ID range

assertions.name: removal_explained
assertions.description: Agent explains that MUXF removals mean synthesis was aggressive
assertions.check: Output explains that removals indicate synthesis MUXF inference was too aggressive and opt_design is correcting

assertions.name: log_scoped_correctly
assertions.description: Log extraction was scoped to the opt_design section only
assertions.check: Agent used sed -n scoping with Command: opt_design markers

evals.name: set-logic-critical-warning
evals.prompt: I'm getting a CRITICAL WARNING [Opt 31-81] about set_logic_one on a pin that's already driven. What does this mean and should I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies [Opt 31-81] as a set_logic constraint on an already-driven pin, explains the constraint is ineffective, and recommends removing the constraint or fixing the netlist.

assertions.name: critical_warning_identified
assertions.description: Agent identifies [Opt 31-81] as set_logic on driven pin
assertions.check: Output explains that set_logic_one/set_logic_zero was applied to an already-driven pin

assertions.name: recommendation_given
assertions.description: Agent recommends removing the constraint or fixing the netlist
assertions.check: Output recommends removing the set_logic constraint or fixing the design intent

evals.name: bram-memory-optimization
evals.prompt: I see [Opt 31-2042] messages in my opt_design log about BRAM memory optimization. What did opt_design do to the BRAMs?
evals.expected_output: Agent explains [Opt 31-2042] relates to BRAM memory optimization (port mapping, power mode conversion), uses scoped grep to extract relevant messages, and checks for bram_power_opt directive usage.

assertions.name: bram_id_recognized
assertions.description: Agent recognizes [Opt 31-2042] as BRAM memory optimization
assertions.check: Output explains that [Opt 31-2042] relates to BRAM port optimization or power mode conversion

assertions.name: log_scoped_correctly
assertions.description: Log extraction was scoped to the opt_design section
assertions.check: Agent used sed -n scoping, not full-log grep

evals.name: hfn-bufg-insertion-review
evals.prompt: opt_design inserted several BUFGs for high-fanout nets. How can I see which nets got BUFGs and control the fanout threshold?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts [Opt 31-194] messages showing BUFG insertions with load counts, explains -hier_fanout_limit directive, and reports the BUFG phase summary from [Opt 31-662].

assertions.name: bufg_messages_extracted
assertions.description: Agent extracts BUFG insertion messages with load counts
assertions.check: Output shows [Opt 31-194] BUFG insertions with specific net names and load counts

assertions.name: fanout_threshold_explained
assertions.description: Agent explains -hier_fanout_limit directive
assertions.check: Output mentions -hier_fanout_limit with minimum value of 512

evals.name: resynth-remap-stats
evals.prompt: I ran opt_design with -remap. What did the resynth/remap phase accomplish? I see Opt 31-2117 and 31-2118 messages.
evals.expected_output: Agent explains [Opt 31-2117] and [Opt 31-2118] as resynth/remap optimization stats, reports LUT packing improvements, and compares with non-remap run.

assertions.name: resynth_ids_recognized
assertions.description: Agent recognizes resynth/remap message IDs
assertions.check: Output explains [Opt 31-2117] and [Opt 31-2118] as resynth/remap optimization counts

assertions.name: log_scoped_correctly
assertions.description: Log scoped to opt_design section
assertions.check: Agent used sed -n scoping to extract only the opt_design section

evals.name: mbufg-gt-sweep-drc
evals.prompt: After opt_design sweeps MBUFG_GT instances I get DRC REQP-2090 about CLR/CLRB_LEAF pins. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies DRC REQP-2090 as an MBUFG_GT CLR/CLRB_LEAF pin issue after sweep, references AR73639, and recommends checking CLR sequencing.

assertions.name: drc_recognized
assertions.description: Agent recognizes DRC REQP-2090 as MBUFG_GT CLR/CLRB_LEAF issue
assertions.check: Output identifies REQP-2090 as related to MBUFG_GT CLR/CLRB_LEAF pin state after sweep

assertions.name: workaround_provided
assertions.description: Agent provides AR reference or workaround
assertions.check: Output references AR73639 or provides guidance for CLR sequencing fix

evals.name: lut-decomposition-analysis
evals.prompt: I see [Opt 31-2244] messages about LUT decomposition. What does this optimization do and is it helping my timing?
evals.expected_output: Agent explains LUT decomposition (LUT6→LUT5+LUT5) for timing improvement, extracts [Opt 31-2244] stats showing decomposition counts, and notes it trades area for timing.

assertions.name: decomposition_explained
assertions.description: Agent explains LUT decomposition purpose
assertions.check: Output explains decomposing wide LUTs (LUT6 to LUT5+LUT5) to improve timing at the cost of area

assertions.name: stats_extracted
assertions.description: Agent extracts decomposition stats from log
assertions.check: Output references [Opt 31-2244] LUT decomposition counts from the scoped log

evals.name: series-ibuf-warning
evals.prompt: opt_design reports [Opt 31-83] about series input buffers. What does this mean for my design?
evals.expected_output: Agent explains [Opt 31-83] detects chained IBUF→IBUF or OBUF→OBUF, recommends RTL fix to eliminate buffer chains.

assertions.name: series_buffer_explained
assertions.description: Agent explains series buffer detection
assertions.check: Output explains that [Opt 31-83] means chained I/O buffers (IBUF→IBUF or OBUF→OBUF) were detected

assertions.name: rtl_fix_recommended
assertions.description: Agent recommends RTL fix
assertions.check: Output recommends fixing RTL to avoid chained I/O buffers
